title: AnOldBabylonian coefficient, its origin and impact on our understanding of measures on circles, including the radian measure
summary: This study reconstructs the origin of a constant, here called $Ξ$ (Xi), as a primary scaling factor in Old Babylonian mathematics and astronomy. $Ξ$ arises from the practical necessity of precise measurements on the sky or a circle, through the harmonization of length-measure systems. The analysis of the Nippur measure (with its famous cubit) and the Gudea measure shows that $Ξ= 375/360$ represents the ratio of these established Old Babylonian measure systems.
